gcloud.title: Google Cloud
gcloud.description: Google Cloud console APIs: projects, service enablement, API keys, billing, monitoring, storage, BigQuery and IAM, plus the rest of the infrastructure, data, devops, networking, security and governance APIs.

notes.cloud_project_iam_policy: Google's IAM server reads deny policies and roles, not who holds a role on a project. Kept because that is the first IAM question; Resource Manager's getIamPolicy, a read.
notes.bq_table_preview: No tool of Google's BigQuery server reads rows without a query. Kept: tabledata.list, which has no query cost.
notes.bq_query_read: A dry run first refuses any statement that is not a SELECT, so it stays a read; bigquery_jobs_query (execute_sql) runs any statement and asks first.
notes.billing_services_list: Google's get_service has no method in Cloud Billing v1; the list covers it.
notes.billing_services_skus_list: Google's get_sku has no method in Cloud Billing v1; the list covers it, and billing_price_lookup finds SKUs by words.
notes.billing_price_lookup: Prices of one SKU (v1beta skus.price.get), or SKUs of a service found by words and region with their list prices, and a billing account's own prices (v1beta billingAccounts.skus.price.get). Google's SKU-group and billing-account SKU and service listings are reached with the gateway (api_call) in the all toolset.
notes.iam_roles_list: Reads only. Google's create_role, update_role, delete_role and undelete_role (IAM v1) are reached with the gateway (api_call) in the all toolset. IAM lists only the cloud-platform scope for roles, so a readonly login cannot run it.
notes.iam_role_get: IAM lists only the cloud-platform scope for roles, so a readonly login cannot run it.
notes.logging_entries_list: Google's list_log_names, list_buckets, list_views (and the observability server's sinks and log scopes) are reached with the gateway (api_call) in the all toolset. Without a time limit the last day is searched, as gcloud logging read does.
notes.monitoring_query_promql: Also runs instant queries (Prometheus /query) when no range is given. Our kind is read, as Google marks query_range; since 1.24.5 the gateway's Prometheus POST queries (query, query_range, query_exemplars, series, labels) are reads too (config/tool-kinds.json).
notes.gcs_read_text: Google's read_text is deprecated in favour of read_object; kept for text, decoded with the object's charset.
notes.gcs_write_text: Unlike Google's write_text it does not replace an existing object unless overwrite is true (ifGenerationMatch=0). It also uploads a local file (local_path).

gsc.title: Search Console
gsc.description: Search Console sites, sitemaps, search analytics, URL indexing and site verification.

google.source: No official Google MCP server for Search Console was found (Google's Cloud and Workspace MCP lists, 2026-10-29; a negative, not confirmed by Google); a lean set chosen here.

notes.sc_sites_list: The properties the account can see, with its permission level. Start here.
notes.sc_site_get: One property and the account's permission on it.
notes.sc_search_analytics_query: Clicks, impressions, CTR and position by query, page, country, device, date or search appearance. A read, as the generated searchcons_searchanalytics_query is since 1.24.5 (config/tool-kinds.json; before, the POST query was a write by its name).
notes.sc_url_inspect: The index status of one URL: coverage, last crawl, canonical, mobile usability and rich results.
notes.sc_sitemaps_list: The sitemaps of a property with their submitted and indexed counts (the indexed count can lag; check a sample with sc_url_inspect).
notes.sc_sitemap_get: One sitemap: its status, errors, warnings and counts.
notes.sc_sitemap_submit: Submits or resubmits a sitemap. A write, so it asks first.
notes.indexing_url_notifications_get_metadata: When the Indexing API was last told about a URL. Needs the indexing scope, which has no read-only form.
notes.indexing_url_notifications_publish: Tells Google a URL was updated or deleted. Google accepts it only for pages with JobPosting or BroadcastEvent (in a VideoObject) markup. A write, so it asks first.

gsearch.title: Search and Web Quality
gsearch.description: Public search and web-quality APIs (Custom Search, PageSpeed, CrUX, Safe Browsing, Web Risk, Fact Check) that take an API key instead of OAuth. The Custom Search JSON API is closed to new customers and is scheduled to be discontinued on 2027-01-01.

notes.developerk_documents_search_documen: Searches Google's developer documentation (Developer Knowledge API searchDocumentChunks): matching chunks with their document names.
notes.developerk_documents_batch_get: The full text of up to 20 documents by name (Developer Knowledge API documents.batchGet), after a search.
notes.developerk_v1_answer_query: A grounded answer about Google developer products (Developer Knowledge API answerQuery). Google marks it read-only, and since 1.24.2 (D2) the suite counts it as a read too, so it does not ask.
notes.pagespeedo_pagespeedap_runpagespeed: No official Google MCP server covers PageSpeed Insights; kept for the Lighthouse scores and Core Web Vitals of a page (PageSpeed Insights API runpagespeed).
notes.chromeuxre_records_query_record: No official Google MCP server covers the Chrome UX Report; kept for real-user Core Web Vitals of an origin or URL (CrUX API records.queryRecord).
notes.kgsearch_entities_search: No official Google MCP server covers the Knowledge Graph; kept to look up an entity by name (Knowledge Graph Search API entities.search).
notes.factcheckt_claims_search: No official Google MCP server covers Fact Check Tools; kept to find published fact checks of a claim (Fact Check Tools API claims.search).
notes.webrisk_uris_search: No official Google MCP server covers Web Risk; kept to check a URL against Google's threat lists (Web Risk API uris.search).

gdrive.title: Google Drive and Docs
gdrive.description: Google Drive files, labels and activity, plus Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms and Books.

notes.drive_search: Takes Drive's own query syntax (q), not the dialect of Google's search_files (title, parentId, owner); the same searches can be written in either.
notes.drive_read_text: PDF and image text is not read: Drive has no public text-extraction call. Office and OpenDocument text is taken from the downloaded file, since Drive exports only Google files.
notes.drive_create_file: Converts to a Google type only when google_type is given; Google's create_file converts by default.
notes.sheets_write_values: One tool for Google's update_values and update_formulas: value_input data (RAW) or formulas (USER_ENTERED), always given.
notes.docs_documents_get: Generated from Docs' documents.get: the full document JSON. Comments (Google's commentsIncluded) are in drive_read_text with include_comments.
notes.slides_presentatio_pages_get_thumbnai: The generated name is cut to fit the 64-character tool name budget.

gmail.title: Gmail
gmail.description: Gmail mailboxes, messages, labels and settings, plus Gmail Postmaster Tools.

notes.gmail_search: Searches messages; Google's search_threads returns threads, as gmail_search_threads does.
notes.gmail_get_attachment: Google's get_message lists attachment ids, but no tool of Google's server downloads them. Kept so the ids lead somewhere; it is a read.
notes.gmail_send_draft: Google's Gmail server has no send tool. Kept so a draft made with gmail_create_draft can be sent; it is destructive, so it asks first.
notes.gmail_label: One tool for threads and messages (label_thread and label_message in Google's server). Trash and Spam are refused here, as Google's label tools refuse them.
notes.gmail_unlabel: One tool for threads and messages (unlabel_thread and unlabel_message in Google's server). Taking mail out of Trash is gmail_untrash.
notes.gmail_trash: Google's label tools send Trash and Spam to tools outside its public list. Kept so mail can still go to Trash; it is destructive, so it asks first and shows what moves.
notes.gmail_untrash: Restores what gmail_trash moved, as removing the Trash label would in Google's server.

gcalendar.title: Google Calendar
gcalendar.description: Google Calendar calendars, events and calendar settings.

notes.calendar_list_events: Google's search_events is a semantic search of the primary calendar with no public API; the keyword search of calendar_list_events (q) stands in for it. Without time_min the list starts now, as before 1.8.0; include_past gives Google's no-lower-bound list.
notes.calendar_suggest_time: Computed here from free/busy (freebusy.query) and the window, duration and working hours given; Google's preferences object is not public, so its exact ranking is not copied.
notes.calendar_delete_event: Destructive, so it asks first, as in Google's server (destructiveHint).

gchat.title: Google Chat
gchat.description: Google Chat spaces, messages and members, plus Workspace Events subscriptions.

notes.chat_list_members: Curated in place of the generated chat_spaces_members_list, whose scope list also names the Chat app scopes chat.bot and chat.import; the greedy readwrite cover would ask a person to grant chat.bot. chat_list_members lists only chat.memberships and chat.memberships.readonly.
notes.chat_send_message: Text in Markdown (or Chat's own syntax), as a new thread or a reply. Google's cards and citations are left out: only Chat apps can post them.
notes.chat_mark_read: Conversations only, up to 10 a call, each its own request with its own failure. Google's thread_ids have no public REST method (the Chat API has getThreadReadState only).
notes.chat_mark_unread: Conversations only; a thread's read state has no public REST method.
notes.chat_users_spaces_space_notificat_patch: Generated from spaceNotificationSetting.patch: name is users/me/spaces/{space}/spaceNotificationSetting, updateMask notification_setting and/or mute_setting. A write, so it asks first.

gmeet.title: Google Meet
gmeet.description: Google Meet spaces, conference records, participants and recordings.

google.source: No official Google MCP server for Google Meet was found (Google's Cloud and Workspace MCP lists, 2026-10-29; a negative, not confirmed by Google); a lean set chosen here.

notes.meet_spaces_create: Makes a new meeting space and returns its meeting link and code. A write, so it asks first.
notes.meet_spaces_get: A meeting space by its name (spaces/{space}) or meeting code: its link, code and settings.
notes.meet_conference_records_list: Past and current conferences (one per meeting held in a space), newest first; filter by space or time. Start here for a meeting that took place.
notes.meet_conference_records_get: One conference: its space, start and end time.
notes.meet_conference_recor_participants_list: Who joined a conference, with join and leave times.
notes.meet_conference_record_transcripts_list: The transcripts of a conference and their Google Docs.
notes.meet_conference_transcript_entries_list: The spoken text of a transcript, entry by entry with the speaker and time.
notes.meet_conference_records_recordings_list: The recordings of a conference and their Drive files.
notes.meet_conference_record_smart_notes_list: The notes Gemini took in a conference (smart notes) and their Google Docs.
notes.meet_conference_records_smart_notes_get: One smart notes entry and the Google Doc that holds it.

gcontacts.title: Contacts and Profile
gcontacts.description: Google Contacts and People, personal health metrics, Data Portability, and the OAuth2 userinfo endpoints.

notes.contacts_search_directory: Sets the readMask (names, email addresses, phone numbers, organizations) and the source (domain profiles) that the generated people_people_search_directory needs from the caller. Carries Google's caution: confirm the person before a result goes into another tool.
notes.contacts_search: Sends the empty warm-up search Google asks for before each search, then the search, with a default readMask. Carries Google's caution.
notes.profile_me: From the OAuth2 userinfo endpoint. Every sign-in holds userinfo.email, so the email is always there; the name needs userinfo.profile, which a readonly login does not ask for (it is not a read-only scope by name).

gtasks.title: Tasks and Keep
gtasks.description: Google Tasks task lists and tasks, plus Google Keep notes.

google.source: No official Google MCP server for Google Tasks or Google Keep was found (Google's Cloud and Workspace MCP lists, 2026-10-29; a negative, not confirmed by Google); a lean set chosen here.

notes.tasks_tasklists_list: Your task lists and their ids. Start here; @default is your first list.
notes.tasks_tasks_list: The tasks of one list, with due dates and status; showCompleted and dueMin/dueMax narrow it.
notes.tasks_tasks_get: One task with its notes, due date, status and links.
notes.tasks_tasks_insert: Adds a task to a list (as a subtask with parent). A write, so it asks first.
notes.tasks_tasks_patch: Changes only the fields given: title, notes, due date, or status completed. A write, so it asks first.
notes.tasks_tasks_delete: Deletes a task. Destructive, so it asks twice.
notes.keep_notes_list: Google Keep notes, read only here (filter by trashed or create and update time). Google documents the Keep API for Google Workspace; whether a personal account can use it is not verified.
notes.keep_notes_get: One Keep note with its text or list items.

gclassroom.title: Google Classroom
gclassroom.description: Google Classroom courses, coursework, submissions, students and teachers.

notes.classroom_get_course: One course by id, with its description and links. Google's list_courses returns these fields per course and has no get; kept so a known course id needs no list.
notes.classroom_list_coursework: Assignments, questions and materials of a course in one list (courseWork.list and courseWorkMaterials.list), published only unless include_drafts; include_submission_overview adds one studentSubmissions.list per item. Materials need a classroom.courseworkmaterials scope; without one the answer lists the coursework and says so.
notes.classroom_cour_cour_list_1590: Generated from courseWorkMaterials.list. Kept so a readonly login of this toolset asks for classroom.courseworkmaterials.readonly, which classroom_list_coursework needs for the materials (one tool can declare only one any-of scope list).
notes.classroom_cour_cour_crea_e311: Generated from courseWork.create (assignments and questions): a raw CourseWork body. Classroom makes it a DRAFT unless state is set. Not curated in this release.
notes.classroom_cour_cour_crea_3302: Generated from courseWorkMaterials.create (materials): a raw CourseWorkMaterial body. Classroom makes it a DRAFT unless state is set.
notes.classroom_cour_cour_patc_dea2: Generated from courseWork.patch: updateMask names the fields to change.
notes.classroom_cours_course_modify: Generated from courseWork.modifyAssignees: adds or removes the students of a coursework item.
notes.classroom_cour_cour_patc_480d: Generated from courseWorkMaterials.patch: updateMask names the fields to change.
notes.classroom_create_rubric: Google's learningGoalId comes from search_course_standards, which has no public REST method (no learning-standards method in Classroom v1 Discovery), so no tool here matches search_course_standards. Google takes rubrics only for coursework of the same Cloud project.

gapps.title: Apps Script
gapps.description: Apps Script projects and execution, plus the Workspace Marketplace SDK.

google.source: No official Google MCP server for Apps Script was found (Google's Cloud and Workspace MCP lists, 2026-10-29; a negative, not confirmed by Google); a lean set chosen here.

notes.appsscript_projects_get: A script project's title, parent file and times, by script id.
notes.appsscript_projects_get_content: The files of a script project: name, type and source.
notes.appsscript_projects_update_content: Replaces every file of a script project with the files given. Destructive since 1.26.3 (Google: it clears all the existing files), so it asks twice; send the files you keep too.
notes.appsscript_projects_versions_create: Saves the current code as a numbered version, for a deployment. A write, so it asks first.
notes.appsscript_projects_deployments_list: The deployments of a script project and their entry points.
notes.appsscript_projects_deployments_create: Deploys a version (as an API executable, web app or add-on, by its manifest). A write, so it asks first.
notes.appsscript_processes_list: Your recent script runs: function, status, start time and duration.
notes.appsscript_scripts_run: Runs a function of a script deployed as an API executable. Destructive, so it asks twice: the script can do anything its own scopes allow, and the sign-in needs those scopes (the login asks for one of them here, userinfo.email).

gadmin.title: Workspace Admin
gadmin.description: Google Workspace administration: Cloud Identity, Chrome management and policy, Groups Settings, licensing, reports, alerts, Vault, reseller and Cloud Search admin.

google.source: No official Google MCP server for Google Workspace administration (the Admin SDK, reports and the alert center) was found in Google's Workspace and Cloud MCP lists on 2026-10-29; a lean set chosen here.

notes.admin_users_list: The domain's users, searchable by name or email (Directory API users.list). Start here for a user key.
notes.admin_user_get: One user, with the groups they belong to (Directory API users.get and groups.list).
notes.admin_groups_list: The account's groups, or the groups of one user (Directory API groups.list).
notes.admin_group_members_list: The members of a group and their roles (Directory API members.list).
notes.admin_domains_list: The domains of the account (Directory API domains.list).
notes.admin_activities_list: Audit activity of the domain: logins, admin console changes, Drive and others (Reports API activities.list).
notes.alerts_alerts_list: Security and system alerts of the domain (Alert Center API alerts.list).
notes.admin_user_set_suspended: Suspends or restores a user. A write: it asks first.
notes.admin_group_member_add: Adds a member to a group. A write: it asks first.

ganalytics.title: Google Analytics
ganalytics.description: Google Analytics admin and data APIs for GA4 properties, configuration and reports.

notes.gaadmin_account_summarie_list: The accounts and properties the signed-in user can see (Admin API v1beta accountSummaries.list). Start here for a property id.
notes.gaadmin_properties_get: One property's details: name, time zone, currency, industry, service level (Admin API v1beta).
notes.gaadmin_propert_google_a_list: The Google Ads accounts linked to a property (Admin API v1beta).
notes.gadata_properties_get_metadat: Every dimension and metric the property can report on, custom ones flagged with customDefinition; Google's tool returns only the custom ones. Pass name properties/<id>/metadata.
notes.ga_run_report: A report with rows keyed by dimension and metric name, row_count, next_offset and, on request, the property's quota. With conversion_spec it runs Google's conversions report on Data API v1alpha, as run_conversions_report does.
notes.ga_run_realtime_report: The last 30 minutes. The Data API has no offset for realtime reports, so there is none here (Google's tool lists one).
notes.ga_run_funnel_report: Data API v1alpha runFunnelReport, which no generated tool or gateway method of this server reaches; steps as event names or filter expressions.
notes.ga_annotations_list: Admin API v1alpha, which the generated tools do not cover (it is a gateway API here).
notes.ga_annotation_create: A write: it asks first, and the approval shows the exact annotation. Needs analytics.edit, which Google's server asks for only with --allow-write.

gtm.title: Tag Manager
gtm.description: Google Tag Manager accounts, containers, tags, triggers and variables.

google.source: No official Google MCP server for Google Tag Manager was found (Google's Cloud and Workspace MCP lists and Google's GitHub organisations, 2026-10-29; a negative, not confirmed by Google); a lean set chosen here.

notes.tagmgr_accounts_list: The Tag Manager accounts the signed-in user can see. Start here.
notes.tagmgr_accounts_containers_list: The containers of an account (web, iOS, Android, AMP, server) with their public ids (GTM-XXXX).
notes.tagmgr_accounts_containers_workspaces_li: The workspaces of a container. Changes are made in a workspace, saved as a version, then published.
notes.tagmgr_accounts_containe_workspace_tags_: One tag with its type, parameters and firing and blocking triggers.
notes.tagmgr_account_contain_workspa_triggers_: One trigger with its type and filters.
notes.tagmgr_account_contain_workspa_variabl_l: The user-defined variables of a workspace.
notes.tagmgr_account_contain_workspa_variable_: One variable with its type and parameters.
notes.tagmgr_accounts_containers_versions_live: The version that is live now, with its tags, triggers and variables.
notes.tagmgr_accounts_containers_version_hea_l: The versions of a container as headers: name, number and counts.
notes.tagmgr_accounts_containe_workspac_create: Saves a workspace as a new container version, and Google deletes the workspace. Destructive since 1.26.3, so it asks twice; nothing goes live.
notes.tagmgr_accounts_containers_versions_publ: Publishes a version: it goes live on every site or app that loads the container. Destructive since 1.26.3, so it asks twice; check the version before.

gyoutube.title: YouTube and Blogger
gyoutube.description: YouTube Data, YouTube Analytics and YouTube Reporting APIs, plus Blogger.

google.source: No official Google MCP server for YouTube was found (Google's Cloud and Workspace MCP lists and Google's GitHub organisations, 2026-10-29; a negative, not confirmed by Google); a lean set chosen here.

notes.youtube_search_list: Search YouTube for videos, channels and playlists. Each call costs 100 units of the project's daily YouTube quota.
notes.youtube_channels_list: Channels by id, by handle, or your own (mine): statistics and the id of the uploads playlist.
notes.youtube_videos_list: Videos by id, or the most popular chart: title, description, statistics and duration.
notes.youtube_playlists_list: The playlists of a channel, or by id.
notes.youtube_playlist_items_list: The videos of a playlist; a channel's uploads playlist lists all its videos.
notes.youtube_comment_threads_list: Top-level comments of a video or channel, with replies. Discovery lists only youtube.force-ssl for it, which has no read-only form, so a readonly login does not cover it.
notes.youtube_captions_list: The caption tracks of a video (not their text). Needs youtube.force-ssl, like the comment threads.
notes.ytanalyt_reports_query: YouTube Analytics for your channel: views, watch time, subscribers and more, by day, video or country.
notes.youtube_videos_update: Changes a video's title, description, tags, category or privacy. Destructive since 1.26.3, so it asks twice: the change is public, and Google deletes a value the request leaves out, so send the whole part.
notes.youtube_comments_insert: Posts a reply to a comment (parentId); a new top-level comment is commentThreads.insert, in the all toolset. A write, so it asks first; the reply is public.

gbusiness.title: Business Profile
gbusiness.description: Business Profile accounts, locations, verifications, lodging, place actions, notifications and performance.

google.source: No official Google MCP server for Google Business Profile was found (Google's Cloud and Workspace MCP lists and Google's GitHub organisations, 2026-10-29; a negative, not confirmed by Google); a lean set chosen here.

notes.mbaccount_accounts_list: The Business Profile accounts the signed-in user can manage. Start here. Google's Business Profile Discovery documents list no OAuth scope; since 1.24.1 the product declares business.manage for them (scopeOverrides), so a readwrite login asks for it. It has no read-only form, so a readonly login covers none of these tools.
notes.mbinfo_accounts_locations_list: The locations of an account; readMask names the fields to return, such as name,title,storefrontAddress.
notes.mbinfo_locations_get: One location with the fields readMask names: hours, categories, phone, website and so on.
notes.bpperf_locations_get_daily_metr: One daily metric of a location over a date range, such as calls or website clicks.
notes.bpperf_locations_fetch_multi_da: Several daily metrics of a location over a date range in one call.
notes.bpperf_loca_sear_impr_mont_list: The search keywords that showed the location, with monthly impressions.
notes.mbverify_location_verifica_list: The verifications of a location and their state.
notes.mbinfo_locations_patch: Changes the fields updateMask names. A write, so it asks first; the change is public on Google Search and Maps.

gads.title: Ads and Publisher
gads.description: Google Ads API (accounts, campaigns, ad groups, ads, keywords, budgets, conversions, assets and GAQL reporting, with every other method through the gateway), plus advertising and publisher APIs: Search Ads 360, Display & Video 360, Campaign Manager, Ad Exchange, AdSense, AdMob, Real-time Bidding and more.

notes.ads_list_customers: The customer resource names the signed-in user can reach; the digits are the customer_id of the other tools. Google's server exposes it as customers_list_accessible_customers.
notes.ads_search: One page of GAQL, at most 500 rows, given as text or as fields, resource, conditions, orderings and limit (Google's structured form, with PARAMETERS omit_unselected_resource_names=true). It calls googleAds:search, not searchStream, and never sends pageSize. Google's server is read-only, so ads_mutate (validate first, then gated changes) is not in this list; it stays in the all and curated toolsets. The manager account is GSM_ADS_LOGIN_CUSTOMER_ID, not a per-call login_customer_id.
notes.ads_resource_metadata: The two field queries Google's get_resource_metadata runs (the resource's attributes, then every field selectable with it), as selectable, filterable and sortable name lists.

gmerchant.title: Merchant Center
gmerchant.description: Merchant Center: Merchant API, Comparison Shopping Service and Manufacturer Center.

notes.merchantap_accounts_list: The Merchant Center accounts the service account can reach (accounts.list). Start here for an account id.
notes.merchantap_accounts_issues_list: Account-level issues that affect the whole account.
notes.merchantap_account_program_list: Programs, such as free listings and Shopping ads, with their state, regions and unmet requirements.
notes.merchantap_accoun_automa_get_au: Automatic improvement settings: item updates, image improvements and shipping improvements.
notes.merchantap_acco_produ_list_6ad8: The products of an account, a page at a time (products.list; the name ends in a hash because of the 64-character budget).
notes.merchantap_account_products_get: One product by its exact resource name, accounts/{account}/products/{product}.
notes.merchantap_account_aggrega_list: Product issues aggregated by reporting context and country, for the health of the product data.
notes.merchantap_accoun_report_search: A Merchant reports query (product performance, statuses, price insights, competitive visibility) in the Merchant Center Query Language.
notes.merchantap_account_data_so_list: The data sources of an account.
notes.merchantap_accoun_data_s_create: Creates a data source. A write, so it asks first.
notes.merchantap_accoun_data_so_fetch: Fetches and processes a data source's file now. Google says it triggers processing, so since 1.24.2 (D2) the suite counts it as a write, and it asks first.
notes.merchantap_accou_data_file_get: The latest file upload of a data source and its processing state (accounts/{account}/dataSources/{datasource}/fileUploads/latest).

gplay.title: Google Play
gplay.description: Google Play developer publishing and reporting, Play Games Services, Android Enterprise and Management, Play Integrity and device APIs.

notes.androidmgmt_list_enterprises: Android Management API, called directly (a gateway API here); the service-account key asks for its scope since 1.23.1. The service account must belong to the project that manages the enterprises.
notes.androidpub_reviews_list: No official Google MCP server covers Play publishing; kept for the app's recent user reviews (Play Developer API reviews.list).
notes.androidpub_reviews_reply: Replies to a user review; the reply is public. A write: it asks first.
notes.androidpub_applica_tracks_releases_list: The releases of a track (production, beta, ...) without opening an edit (applications.tracks.releases.list).
notes.androidpub_edits_tracks_list: The tracks of an edit; it needs an edit id, which androidpub_edits_insert (a write) opens.
notes.androidpub_purchases_subscriptionsv_get: One subscription purchase by its token (purchases.subscriptionsv2.get).

gfirebase.title: Firebase
gfirebase.description: Firebase management, App Check, App Distribution, Crashlytics, Hosting, Data Connect, Rules, Test Lab, FCM and Identity Toolkit.

notes.firebase_projects_search_apps: Every app of a project (iOS, Android and web) in one list; Google's tool filters by platform.
notes.firebase_projec_web_app_get_con: The web app's SDK configuration; Google's one tool takes the platform, here there is one tool per platform.
notes.firebaseru_project_release_list: The rules releases of a project; with firebaseru_project_rulesets_get it gives the rules source, as Google's tool does. Realtime Database rules are not covered (no API here).
notes.firebaseru_projects_test: Checks a rules source. Google marks it read-only, and since 1.24.2 (D2) the suite counts it as a read too, so it does not ask.
notes.firebaseap_proj_locat_backe_get: The backend and its state. Google's tool also reads its build and run logs, which are Cloud Logging: use the gcloud server's logging_entries_list.
notes.firebaseda_pro_loc_ser_sch_list: The schemas of a Data Connect service; Google's list_services returns them with the services.
notes.firebaseda_pro_loc_ser_con_list: The connectors of a Data Connect service; Google's list_services returns them with the services.
notes.firebaseda_pro_loc_ser_exe_1fce: Runs any GraphQL operation, mutations too. A write, so it asks first.

gmaps.title: Maps and Location

notes.places_places_search_text: Places API (New) searchText: places by a text query, with an optional location bias. Google's search_places also returns a summary written by its server; this returns Places data.

notes.googleads: Generated: 33 per-method tools for the core Google Ads resources, in this order: accounts (listAccessibleCustomers, mutate, createCustomerClient), GAQL search and searchStream, googleAdsFields, campaigns and campaign budgets, account budget proposals, ad groups, ads and ad group ads, keywords (ad group and campaign criteria, negative keywords, keyword ideas, keyword theme and geo target suggestions), conversion actions and goals, bidding strategies, and assets (asset groups, asset sets, and the account, campaign and ad group asset links). The include list is a list of resource or method paths: a path names every method of a resource, or one method. The other 141 methods (reporting forecasts, audiences, experiments, labels, batch jobs and so on) are reached through the gateway with api_search, api_describe and api_call. Media upload is not supported by the gateway. Every mutate method is dynamic: validateOnly true is a read, a remove operation is destructive, and any other change is a write.
notes.displayvideo@v4: Generated subset: 116 per-method tools for the advertiser workflow (advertisers, campaigns, insertion orders, line items, ad groups and ad group ads, creatives, ad assets, negative keywords, channels, location lists, targeting options, audiences, invoices, floodlight groups, SDF download tasks and YouTube asset associations). The other 60 methods (partners, users, inventory sources, guaranteed orders, custom bidding, reach forecasts and so on) are reached through the gateway. The whole document is still snapshotted, so every OAuth scope of the API is granted at login.
